vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: parallel
Version: 1.0.6

The OpenClaw AgentSkills skill bundle for Parallel.ai is classified as benign. The code and documentation consistently describe and implement a client for the Parallel.ai API, focusing on web search, research, extraction, and monitoring. There is no evidence of intentional malicious behavior such as data exfiltration (beyond sending API keys to their legitimate endpoints), unauthorized execution, persistence mechanisms, or obfuscation. The `SKILL.md` documentation is clear, functional, and lacks any prompt-injection attempts against the AI agent. Furthermore, the `disable-model-invocation: true` setting in `SKILL.md` prevents autonomous invocation by the agent, requiring explicit user action. All scripts (`scripts/parallel.sh`, `scripts/extract.py`, `scripts/findall.py`, `scripts/monitor.py`, `scripts/search.py`, `scripts/task.py`) correctly handle API keys from environment variables and direct all network traffic to the documented `api.parallel.ai` or `api.browser-use.com` endpoints, without accessing local files or system resources beyond standard output.

llm.summary: The skill's code, required binaries, and environment variables line up with its stated purpose (wrapping the Parallel.ai APIs); nothing in the package asks for unrelated credentials or system access.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Parallel.ai search/research) matches what the files do: scripts call Parallel.ai endpoints for search, task, findall, extract, and monitor workflows. Required binaries (python3, curl, jq) and the primary env var PARALLEL_API_KEY are appropriate for these scripts. No unrelated services/credentials are required.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and included scripts operate only against Parallel.ai (api.parallel.ai / platform.parallel.ai). The monitor script supports user-specified webhook URLs (expected for alerting) and Task supports optional authenticated browsing via browser-use.com when the user provides BROWSERUSE_API_KEY. The scripts do not read local secrets/config paths beyond the declared env vars, and they do not attempt to access system files. Note: providing a webhook or the optional browser-use key will cause data (monitor payloads or fetched page contents) to be sent to external endpoints; this is expected but worth being explicit about.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no automated install spec; SKILL.md recommends pip installing parallel-sdk and requests. No downloads from untrusted URLs or archive extraction are present. The package is instruction/code-only (scripts included), so installation risk is limited to installing the Python dependencies the README suggests.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only PARALLEL_API_KEY is required (declared as primary). Optional envs referenced in docs/scripts: BROWSERUSE_API_KEY (only for authenticated browsing) and PARALLEL_MAX_WAIT (used by parallel.sh). No unrelated or extraneous credentials are requested. Requiring a browser-use key is justified by the documented feature; however supplying that optional key grants the skill the ability to access authenticated pages via the stated third-party MCP server.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not always-enabled (always: false) and model invocation is disabled (disable-model-invocation: true), so it cannot be invoked autonomously by the agent — this reduces risk. The skill does not attempt to modify other skills or system-wide agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears coherent and does what it claims — it wraps Parallel.ai APIs and requires only the Parallel API key. Before installing: (1) Only provide PARALLEL_API_KEY if you trust the Parallel.ai account you will be charging/using; API keys give that service the ability to perform queries on your behalf and may incur usage/costs. (2) If you provide the optional BROWSERUSE_API_KEY, the skill will send that key to api.browser-use.com to enable authenticated page access — only provide it if you trust that third party and the key's scope. (3) Monitor create accepts arbitrary webhook URLs; if you configure one, monitor events (including extracted content) may be POSTed to that external endpoint — avoid untrusted webhooks. (4) The code is readable in the bundle and only calls api.parallel.ai and api.browser-use.com; if you need stronger assurance, run the scripts in an isolated environment (or inspect/execute them manually) and do not export secrets into a global shell before testing. (5) The skill metadata has no homepage/source attribution; if provenance is important, ask the publisher for their identity or the upstream repository before use.
